issue_context.title: REF: in pandas.io.common integerate BytesIOWrapper into IOHandle
issue_context.body:
references:

- [pyarrow CSV engine basic PR](#38370)
- https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/37639#issuecomment-742278895 
- https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/37639#issuecomment-742295452 
- https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/37639#issuecomment-742650316 

pyarrow requires `BytesIO` not `StringIO` so in #38370 we add a class that returns a binary handle to reader input. This class (`BytesIOWrapper`) should be integrated into `IOHandle` to better align with the patterns we use elsewhere for file handles (#37639 is the PR that standardized things)

I originally intended to do this in #38370 but I got a little stuck and since that PR is sizeable already I think it's better to spin it off into a separate follow-on task
comments: Going to be taking this one now. The main use case for this would be pyarrow reading text data, so would be CSV and maybe JSON if we want that in the future.

review_comments: I don't know what pandas's policy is on public/private classes. Maybe name the class `_BytesIOWrapper`. @jreback
this is fine, this entire module is de-facto private.
and we already expose TextIOWrapper so this is similar
That would close/mess up the buffer passed in by the user, which we won't want to touch. I think detach exists for GC purposes, but not sure.

I think this block:
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/42669/files#diff-934d8564d648e7521db673c6399dcac98e45adfd5230ba47d3aabfcc21979febR105
should take care of not closing user-provided file handles?
That calls detach, which is not implemented by BytesIO(the parent class of BytesIOWrapper).
okay, sorry I wasn't aware of that.
Maybe change the comment to something like "the (text) handle is always provided by the caller since get_handle would have opened it in binary mode". I am not sure whether that is clearer.
